run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T09:20:00Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy corresponds to a short burst of gateway 5xx responses on 2026-11-16 between about 09:22:34 and 09:27:06. frontend-proxy ingress spans marked STATUS_CODE_ERROR were 106.495 per 20m against 9632.129 STATUS_CODE_UNSET at 09:40 (about 1.1%), and the 5-minute ingress error ratio rose from at or below 0.0015 to 0.028-0.029 in the 09:24-09:28 windows before returning to 0.0015 at 09:29. frontend-proxy's access log shows the responses: HTTP 500 on POST/GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout starting 09:22:34.371Z, alongside sporadic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}. The errors are confined to cart-dependent routes: frontend's error spans are grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (53.83/20m), CartService/GetCart (23.81), CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (18.63) and tcp.connect (7.25), while frontend (392.347) and frontend-proxy (202.651) account for essentially all error spans and accounting, cart, checkout and payment each recorded 0. The burst begins one second after the single cart pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 was stopped at 09:22:33Z during a Deployment cart rollout: ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d was created 09:22:30Z with kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T09:22:30Z and the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart (Deployment revision 2, 1 replica, maxUnavailable 25%, no readinessProbe). No other workload was rolled out in the window. Cart itself kept serving and logged no application errors, so the observed failure is request-level disruption of frontend's cart calls during pod replacement rather than a cart application fault. A separate fault exists in the same window: the fraud-detection container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 09:28:00Z and restarted, but it post-dates the 500 burst and is not tied to this alert.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's span-metric series in this window are only 'ingress' (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and 'router frontend egress' (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT), each existing with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

In the 20 minutes ending 09:40:00Z, frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans increased by 106.495 with STATUS_CODE_ERROR versus 9632.129 STATUS_CODE_UNSET (about 1.1% of ingress spans marked error), and 'router frontend egress' by 96.156 error versus 9641.435 UNSET, matching the alert's reported magnitude of about 0.0111.

frontend-proxy's 20-minute STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increase was 38.03 at 09:20:00Z and jumped to 202.05 at 09:24:00Z, staying near 199-204 through 09:40:00Z, while the corresponding UNSET increase was 25366.1 at 09:20 and 19273.6 at 09:40.

The 5-minute frontend-proxy ingress error ratio was at or below 0.0015 from 09:07 through 09:23, rose to 0.0283/0.0285/0.0294/0.0290/0.0292 at 09:24-09:28, dropped to 0.0015 at 09:29 and was 0.0045 at 09:38.

Error spans in the 20 minutes ending 09:40:00Z are concentrated in two services: frontend 392.347 and frontend-proxy 202.651; recommendation was 2.070, ad 1.035 and fraud-detection 1.035, while accounting, cart, checkout and payment each recorded 0 error-status spans.

frontend's error spans over that 20-minute window are on cart- and checkout-dependent operations: grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 53.83, CartService/GetCart 23.81, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 18.63, tcp.connect 7.25, POST /api/cart 53.83, GET /api/cart 23.81 and POST /api/checkout 18.63; /api/data, AdService/GetAds and the ProductCatalog/Recommendation calls show 0.

The frontend error-span increase is non-zero only in the 5-minute windows ending 09:25 and 09:27 (CartService/AddItem 57.78, GetCart 25.56, PlaceOrder 20, tcp.connect 7.78, POST /api/cart 57.78, GET /api/cart 25.56, POST /api/checkout 20); all other sampled windows from 09:03 to 09:37 show 0 for these operations.

frontend-proxy's access log shows the first HTTP 500 of the incident at 09:22:34.371Z on 'POST /api/cart' (via_upstream); a scan of 09:15:00-09:22:42Z contains no 5xx between a 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' at 09:18:47.251Z and that 09:22:34.371Z entry.

From 09:22:34 to 09:23:02 frontend-proxy logged repeated 'HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' responses with 21-byte bodies and 1-3 ms upstream times on POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout; later 5xx entries in 09:23:47-09:27:06 are 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on /api/products, /api/data and /api/cart.

Sporadic 5xx existed before the incident: 33 matching 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' lines appeared in frontend-proxy logs for 08:52:00-09:18:00, for example 09:02:14.804Z, 09:03:30.569Z, 09:05:34.515Z, 09:09:04.972Z and 09:11:07.080Z.
After 09:29:00 the gateway logged only one further 5xx in 09:29:00-09:41:00 (a single 503 UC upstream_reset at 09:29:35.559Z), indicating the burst had ended.

Deployment otel-demo/cart was rolled out at 09:22:30Z: new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d was created 2026-11-16T09:22:30Z with annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T09:22:30Z and the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, while cart-755465879b (created 08:51:20Z) was scaled to 0; the cart Deployment is at revision 2.
cart-84889c965d is the only ReplicaSet created in otel-demo after 09:00:00Z; no other Deployment's pod template was replaced in the window.

Namespace events for the rollout: pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz Scheduled 09:22:30Z, cart container Created/Started 09:22:32Z, 'Stopping container cart' and 'Deleted pod: cart-755465879b-rh5r4' at 09:22:33Z, with Deployment/cart 'Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1' at 09:22:30Z and 'Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0' at 09:22:33Z.
The replacement cart pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz is Running and Ready (Ready condition lastTransitionTime 09:22:33Z, created 09:22:30Z) with restartCount 0 for container cart.
Deployment cart runs 1 replica with RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, has no readinessProbe on the cart container, and sets resource limits cpu 45m / memory 165Mi.

Cart continued to serve during and after the pod replacement: the new pod's logs show normal 'AddItemAsync'/'GetCartAsync'/'EmptyCartAsync' entries at 09:24:49-09:24:59, and a filtered search of cart logs for 09:22:30-09:26:00 returned only one match, a benign 'Overriding HTTP_PORTS ...' notice, with no application error lines.

cart's gRPC server spans kept being recorded throughout 09:17-09:35, for example POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 477.6-572 spans per 2m and AddItem 156-318 per 2m, and every cart span series carried STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so cart recorded no error-status spans.

fraud-detection's container was OOMKilled: lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-16T09:28:00Z, restartCount 1, restarted 09:28:01Z in pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh; its Deployment is at revision 1 with a 400Mi memory limit and no readinessProbe.

At query time all 21 otel-demo pods were Running and ready; only fraud-detection showed a restart (restartCount 1), while the frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 had restartCount 0 and start time 08:51:21Z.

The frontend workload was not restarted or rolled out: ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 was created 08:51:21Z with no restartedAt annotation, its image is unchanged ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend, and its pod reports restartCount 0, so a frontend restart does not explain the 5xx burst.

Cart was not continuously down: its server spans continued at normal volume across the burst and its logs show successful AddItem/GetCart handling at 09:24:49Z onward, so the 5xx are better explained as request-level disruption of frontend's cart calls than as a multi-minute cart application failure.

The alert does not reflect a total outage: only about 1.1% of frontend-proxy ingress spans carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and the gateway logged normal 200 'via_upstream' responses for /api/cart, /api/checkout, /api/products and /api/data immediately before and after the burst.

Most likely mechanism: the 09:22:30Z rollout of the single-replica cart Deployment replaced the pod under load; because the cart container has no readinessProbe it was marked Ready as soon as the container started (09:22:33Z) while the old pod was stopped in the same second, so frontend's established gRPC connections to the old cart pod failed and were re-established, consistent with the tcp.connect error spans, the 1-3 ms 21-byte 500 responses on /api/cart and /api/checkout, and the halt of 500s after about 28 seconds.

The pre-existing sporadic 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses from frontend (33 lines in 08:52-09:18, plus one at 09:29:35Z) form a background gateway error floor that likely keeps an 'above 0' alert condition close to firing even outside the incident, but they are too sparse to explain the 09:24-09:28 ratio of about 0.029.

The fraud-detection OOMKill at 09:28:00Z did not trigger this alert: the frontend-proxy 500 burst started at 09:22:34Z and its dense phase ended around 09:23:02Z, before the OOMKill, and no PlaceOrder error spans appear in the window after 09:27 while only one further gateway 5xx was logged after 09:29.

The cart pod was not evicted or crashed: the only pod-level event for the old cart pod is a controller-driven 'Killing'/'SuccessfulDelete' by ReplicaSet cart-755465879b at 09:22:33Z paired with 'Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d' and the restartedAt annotation, and no Evicted or OOMKilled mark appears for cart.

Make the cart workload rollout-safe: add a gRPC readinessProbe to the cart container, set maxUnavailable 0 for the single-replica Deployment (or run 2+ replicas / a PodDisruptionBudget), and verify whether the 45m CPU limit delays startup under the load seen.

Harden frontend's cart/checkout gRPC clients (re-resolution and reconnect with bounded retries and deadlines) so a cart pod replacement stops surfacing as HTTP 500 on /api/cart and /api/checkout, and confirm whether the gateway should retry or map upstream failures away from 5xx.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule itself: its threshold appears to be 'above 0' while frontend-proxy already emits sporadic 503 upstream_reset responses at baseline, so separate routing/connection-reset 503s from application 500s if the rule is meant to track a specific failure class.
Follow up separately on the fraud-detection container being OOMKilled against a 400Mi limit at 09:28:00Z and restarting once, and check its memory profile during the load ramp.

gaps: The exact alert rule could not be verified: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the expression, threshold and the reported value 0.01111111111111111 (exactly 1/90) are unknown; the span-metric ingress error ratio of about 1.1% over 20m only matches the alert's magnitude.
The alert's stated firing time 2026-11-16T09:20:00Z precedes the first observed 5xx at 09:22:34.371Z; this discrepancy (alert evaluation/pending period or metric export lag) could not be resolved.

No trace data covers the burst: the frontend trace search returned spans only through 09:08:26Z and frontend-proxy trace searches for 09:15-09:41Z returned no traces, so the exact gRPC error text and reset reason for the failed cart calls are unknown. The one trace slice read is incomplete and truncated, and the frontend trace search itself failed with RESULT_TOO_LARGE for the wider 08:20-09:41Z query.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines in 09:18-09:30Z (empty results, not proof of absence), so the application-side error behind the 21-byte 500 bodies could not be read.
The old cart pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 was deleted, so its previous-container status, exit codes and logs are unavailable; whether it was fully healthy at termination is unknown.
Who or what triggered the cart rollout at 09:22:30Z is unknown because the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_available returned no series for otel-demo, so deployment availability over time could not be checked; only current Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod objects and events were observable.
valkey-cart logged no lines at all in the window (no_data), so its health during the burst is unverified; no valkey restart or error evidence was observed either.
rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no data for frontend/frontend-proxy, so per-gRPC-status-code error counts could not be obtained.

http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no data for frontend-proxy and its status_code label values were empty, so the gateway's own HTTP metric could not be used to corroborate the alert value.
The origin of the pre-existing sporadic 503 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses (also present before 09:22) is not determined.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition (and any recording rule behind it) from the alerting stack that emitted it, since it is not present in the queried Prometheus.
Review the cart Deployment change that set kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T09:22:30Z in deployment/change history, including who performed it and whether it was intended as remediation.
Read frontend pod logs from a source that retains them for 09:18-09:30Z to capture the exact error behind the cart/checkout 500 responses.
Add a readinessProbe and rollout-safety settings for cart in a change-controlled manner, then observe a controlled cart pod replacement under load to confirm the disruption window shrinks.
Investigate the fraud-detection memory limit and OOMKill separately from this alert.
